source.title: Deep Neural Network Training with Frank-Wolfe
source.authors: Sebastian Pokutta; Christoph Spiegel; Max Zimmer

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on image-classification test accuracy, using different datasets and a different experimental setup than the claim version describes.
record.gate_note: The optimizer comparisons in Figures 8 and 9 report test accuracies for individual single runs. Other comparisons and results on constrained training do not measure a claim version's named behavior.
record.test_reason: Figures 8–9 directly compare adaptive optimizers with SGD using held-out image-classification accuracy, bearing on V4. Figure 4 also reports test error for fully connected and convolutional networks on MNIST, bearing on V3, although its plotted outcomes cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors demonstrate feasible constrained neural-network training with stochastic Frank–Wolfe methods, report that suitable constraints can match regularized SGD performance, and show that constraint choice affects learned representations.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizer test accuracies in single-run MNIST and Fashion-MNIST experiments; it does not implement the claim version's broader benchmark and tuning comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the reported optimizer comparison values; MNIST and Fashion-MNIST results are separate.
record.problems: The optimizer comparison results are single runs without uncertainty estimates; the reported comparisons do not state the tuning procedure and do not report training performance.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable optimizer-comparison rows omitted. Other experiments report constrained-training results or comparisons outside the named claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
The contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, and initialization from trained convolutional networks.

Language benchmarks; deep-network adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons; matched training performance; systematic limited versus broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers. Figures 8–9 provide learning rates but no tuning search procedure or repeated-run uncertainty.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Figure 4 reports MNIST test errors for fully connected and convolutional networks, including standard momentum-SGD conditions with and without weight decay, averaged over five runs. These bear on V3 despite being declared outside the versions in rows_left_out. Add architecture-specific test-error rows and their comparisons. The supplied text preserves axes and legend but no recoverable plotted coordinates, so a directional V3 verdict cannot be assigned.
missing.locator: Section 4.3, Figure 4, and Appendix C opening setup paragraph

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Higher adaptive-optimizer accuracies warrant condition-specific challenges rather than limits_scope solely because runs lack replication. They do not establish that adaptive methods generally outperform SGD. The extraction also incorrectly says learning-rate details are absent; both captions state them.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization on images.

Language benchmarks, multiple runs or uncertainty for the optimizer comparisons, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and comparisons under matched training performance.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its interaction with training set size, data augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: MNIST, no-hidden-layer classifier, 10 epochs, batch size 64, no momentum, single runs at stated learning rates
relationships.reason: R1–R4 report Adam 92.65%, Adagrad 92.42%, and Adadelta 92.55% versus SGD 92.15%; all adaptive methods outperform SGD in these runs, with no uncertainty or tuning-search description.
relationships.display_finding: Adam, Adagrad and Adadelta reportedly exceeded SGD accuracy in the single runs, but these comparisons remain unverified and uncertainty was unreported.
